display.title: Episode 366: The Return of Yehudah, Chapter 11 (Parshas Shekalim)
display.summary_short: What the half-shekel teaches about unity and about staying close to a tzaddik, a Shema guest from Beis Rivka, and Yehudah arrives in a village where the old man's sign comes true.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the week of Parshas Vayakhel and Parshas Shekalim 5749. Uncle Yossi explains that the half-shekel given by every Jew, rich and poor alike, made the silver sockets of the Mishkan: Hashem rests His Presence where there is achdus, and each of us is only half until we join with others, as the Baal Shem Tov taught about loving every Jew. Then another secret of the holy letters: in the word machatzis, the tzaddik in the middle is flanked by ches and yud, spelling chai, life, while the letters further away spell mes; stay close to your teacher and Rebbe to find true life. After the Hakochainik march and a recap of the talis katan with its secret message, a third-grade girl from Beis Rivka leads the Shema. In the story, Yehudah reaches a village where he is warmly welcomed and becomes the rabbi's guest. Between Mincha and Maariv he clearly explains a difficult verse for the simple folk, and the next morning the rabbi asks him to become the town's teacher, the very sign the old man had given him.
display.lesson: Unity brings Hashem's Presence, and staying close to a tzaddik and your teacher brings true life.
